classes.label: Abbreviation Glossary
classes.comment: A listing of abbreviations and acronyms used throughout the SDS, typically found in Section 16.

classes.label: Accidental Release Measure
classes.comment: An action recommended for safely containing and cleaning up a spill or accidental release of the product.
classes.example: :measureX a sds:AccidentalReleaseMeasure ; rdfs:label "Sweep up and place in suitable containers"@en .

classes.label: Acute Toxicity
classes.comment: GHS hazard class covering acute toxic effects via oral, dermal, or inhalation routes.

classes.label: Acute Toxicity - Inhalation
classes.comment: Acute toxicity hazard class specifically for the inhalation route of exposure.

classes.label: Acute Toxicity Inhalation Category 4
classes.comment: GHS classification for substances harmful if inhaled (inhalation route, category 4, H332, Warning signal word).

classes.label: Acute Toxicity - Oral
classes.comment: Acute toxicity hazard class specifically for the oral route of exposure.

classes.label: Acute Toxicity Oral Category 4
classes.comment: GHS classification for substances harmful if swallowed (oral route, category 4, H302, Warning signal word).

classes.label: Administrative Control
classes.comment: A workplace policy or procedure, rather than equipment, used to limit worker exposure to a hazard.
classes.example: :controlX a sds:AdministrativeControl ; rdfs:label "Rotate workers to limit exposure time"@en .

classes.label: Aquatic Chronic Category 2
classes.comment: GHS classification for substances toxic to aquatic life with long lasting effects (chronic, category 2, H411).

classes.label: GHS Hazard Category 1 — Highest Severity
classes.comment: GHS hazard severity category 1 — most severe within a hazard class.

classes.label: GHS Hazard Category 2 — High Severity
classes.comment: GHS hazard severity category 2 — high severity, the second most restrictive tier within a hazard class.

classes.label: GHS Hazard Category 3 — Moderate Severity
classes.comment: GHS hazard severity category 3 — moderate severity, less restrictive than categories 1 and 2.

classes.label: GHS Hazard Category 4 — Low Severity
classes.comment: GHS hazard severity category 4 — least severe in the numbered tier.

classes.label: Chemical Component
classes.comment: Any chemical substance that makes up part of a product's composition, whether or not it is classified as hazardous.

classes.label: Chemical Entity
classes.comment: A chemical substance, compound, polymer, mixture component, decomposition product, or combustion product mentioned in an SDS.

classes.label: Combustion Product
classes.comment: A chemical species generated specifically when the product burns in a fire, often hazardous to inhale.

classes.label: Commercial Product
classes.comment: A finished, market-ready product offering sold under a trademark, as opposed to a raw chemical substance.

classes.label: Composition Record
classes.comment: A structured record connecting a product to a component, concentration, CAS number, and hazard classification.

classes.label: Control Measure
classes.comment: Any engineering, administrative, or personal protective measure used to reduce exposure to a product's hazards.

classes.label: Danger
classes.comment: GHS signal word for the more severe hazard categories.

classes.label: Decomposition Product
classes.comment: A chemical species formed when the product breaks down under heat or other stress, as opposed to during combustion.

classes.label: Ecological Effect
classes.comment: A documented or expected impact of the product on the environment, such as aquatic toxicity.
classes.example: :effectX a sds:EcologicalEffect ; rdfs:label "Toxic to aquatic life"@en .

classes.label: Emergency Contact
classes.comment: A phone number, email, or organization to contact in case of a chemical emergency or accidental exposure.

classes.label: Engineering Control
classes.comment: A physical or mechanical system, such as ventilation, used to reduce worker exposure at its source.

classes.label: Environmental Hazard
classes.comment: A hazard describing the product's or a component's potential to harm aquatic life or the broader environment.

classes.label: Evidence Span
classes.comment: The specific span of source text in the original document that supports an extracted fact or relation.

classes.label: Exposure Limit
classes.comment: A regulatory or recommended airborne concentration threshold for a chemical, such as an OSHA PEL or ACGIH TWA.
classes.example: :limitX a sds:ExposureLimit ; rdfs:label "OSHA PEL TWA 5 mg/m3"@en .

classes.label: Extinguishing Media
classes.comment: A substance, such as water or foam, recommended for extinguishing a fire involving the product.

classes.label: Extraction Record
classes.comment: A record of an extracted entity or relation from OCR, NLP, or ontology-based information extraction.

classes.label: Eye Protection
classes.comment: PPE designed to shield the eyes from splashes, dust, or vapor exposure.
classes.example: :ppeX a sds:EyeProtection ; rdfs:label "Safety glasses with side-shields"@en .

classes.label: Fire-Fighting Measure
classes.comment: Guidance for safely extinguishing or responding to a fire involving the product.
classes.example: :measureX a sds:FireFightingMeasure ; rdfs:label "Fight fire from a safe distance"@en .

classes.label: First Aid Measure
classes.comment: A recommended action to take immediately after a person is exposed to or injured by the product.
classes.example: :measureX a sds:FirstAidMeasure ; rdfs:label "Flush eyes with water for 15 minutes"@en .

classes.label: GHS Classification
classes.comment: A GHS hazard classification, including hazard class, category, and hazard statement.

classes.label: Hand Protection
classes.comment: PPE specifically intended to protect the hands, such as gloves, during product handling.

classes.label: Handling Requirement
classes.comment: A practice or precaution recommended for safely working with the product during normal use.

classes.label: Hazard
classes.comment: Any potential source of harm associated with the product, encompassing physical, health, environmental, or process hazards.

classes.label: GHS Hazard Category
classes.comment: The numeric severity tier within a GHS hazard class, with lower numbers generally indicating greater severity.

classes.label: GHS Hazard Class
classes.comment: The GHS category describing the type of hazard a substance poses, such as Acute Toxicity or Aquatic Chronic hazard.

classes.label: GHS Hazard Statement
classes.comment: A standardized GHS phrase, identified by an H-code, that describes the nature of a substance's hazard.
classes.example: :h302 a sds:HazardStatement ; sds:ghsCode "H302" ; sds:hazardStatementText "Harmful if swallowed"@en .

classes.label: Hazardous Component
classes.comment: A chemical component that meets GHS criteria for a hazard classification and must be disclosed in Section 3.

classes.label: Hazardous to the Aquatic Environment - Chronic
classes.comment: GHS hazard class for substances with chronic (long-term) aquatic toxicity.

classes.label: Health Hazard
classes.comment: A hazard that can cause adverse health effects in humans through inhalation, skin contact, eye contact, or ingestion.

classes.label: Ingredient
classes.comment: A chemical component intentionally added to a formulation, such as a polymer, additive, or colorant.

classes.label: Chemical Inventory Status
classes.comment: The listing status of a chemical on a national or regional chemical inventory, such as TSCA or EINECS.

classes.label: Legal Disclaimer
classes.comment: A legal notice or limitation-of-liability statement appearing in Section 16 of the SDS.

classes.label: Manufacturer
classes.comment: The organization responsible for producing the product, as distinct from the entity supplying or selling it.

classes.label: Mixture
classes.comment: A product composed of two or more substances combined together, such as a polymer blend with additives.

classes.label: Non-Hazardous Component
classes.comment: A chemical component present in the product that does not meet GHS hazard classification criteria.

classes.label: OCR Block
classes.comment: A contiguous block of text extracted from a scanned or rendered SDS page via optical character recognition.

classes.label: Organization
classes.comment: A company or corporate entity referenced in the SDS, such as the product's manufacturer or supplier.
classes.example: :orgX a sds:Organization ; sds:address "123 Main St, City, Country" .

classes.label: Personal Protective Equipment
classes.comment: Personal protective equipment worn by a worker to reduce exposure to a product's hazards.

classes.label: Physical or Chemical Property
classes.comment: A measurable physical or chemical characteristic of the product, such as density, solubility, or vapor pressure.

classes.label: Physical Hazard
classes.comment: A hazard arising from the physical or chemical properties of the product, such as flammability or dust explosivity.

classes.label: GHS Pictogram
classes.comment: A GHS hazard symbol, such as a flame or exclamation mark, used on labels to visually communicate a hazard type.
classes.example: :exclamationMark a sds:Pictogram ; rdfs:label "GHS exclamation mark pictogram"@en .

classes.label: Polymer
classes.comment: A high molecular weight chemical entity built from repeating monomer units, such as the resin matrix of a plastic product.

classes.label: GHS Precautionary Statement
classes.comment: A standardized GHS phrase, identified by a P-code, recommending measures to minimize or prevent exposure to a hazard.
classes.example: :p264 a sds:PrecautionaryStatement ; sds:ghsCode "P264" ; sds:precautionaryStatementText "Wash hands thoroughly after handling"@en .

classes.label: Process Hazard
classes.comment: A hazard that arises specifically during industrial processing of the product, such as melt processing or secondary machining.

classes.label: Product
classes.comment: A product described by an SDS.

classes.label: Reference Listing
classes.comment: A list of standards, regulations, or literature references cited in the SDS, typically found in Section 16.

classes.label: Regulatory Listing
classes.comment: A statement of the product's or a component's status under a specific law or regulatory program, such as SARA or Proposition 65.
classes.example: :listingX a sds:RegulatoryListing ; sds:regulatoryStatusText "Listed: subject to reporting requirements"@en .

classes.label: Respiratory Protection
classes.comment: PPE designed to protect the wearer's airway from inhaling hazardous fumes, dust, or vapors.

classes.label: Revision History
classes.comment: A structured record of changes made to the SDS across document versions, typically listed in Section 16.

classes.label: Route of Exposure
classes.comment: A pathway by which a hazardous substance can enter the body, such as inhalation, skin contact, or ingestion.

classes.label: Safety Data Sheet Document
classes.comment: A safety data sheet document describing a product, mixture, substance, hazards, controls, and regulatory information.

classes.label: SDS Section
classes.comment: A section of a Safety Data Sheet. An SDS is partitioned into exactly 16 sections as defined by the GHS standard; each section is mutually exclusive and together they cover the complete SDS.

classes.label: Section 10 - Stability and Reactivity
classes.comment: The SDS section describing chemical stability, conditions to avoid, and hazardous decomposition products.

classes.label: Section 11 - Toxicological Information
classes.comment: The SDS section reporting toxicological data such as LD50 values, routes of exposure, and carcinogenicity findings.

classes.label: Section 12 - Ecological Information
classes.comment: The SDS section describing the product's potential ecotoxicity and environmental impact.

classes.label: Section 13 - Disposal Considerations
classes.comment: The SDS section providing guidance on proper waste disposal of the product and its packaging.

classes.label: Section 14 - Transport Information
classes.comment: The SDS section stating the product's regulatory transport classification under DOT, IMDG, IATA, and related modal regulations.

classes.label: Section 15 - Regulatory Information
classes.comment: The SDS section listing chemical inventory status (TSCA, DSL, EINECS, etc.) and applicable regulatory programs such as SARA and Prop 65.

classes.label: Section 16 - Other Information
classes.comment: The SDS section containing additional information including revision history, legal disclaimers, and preparer details. Per the GHS SDS standard, this section has no mandated sub-structure and intentionally serves as a structured catch-all.

classes.label: Section 1 - Identification
classes.comment: The SDS section giving product/trade names, supplier, manufacturer, and emergency contact details.

classes.label: Section 2 - Hazards Identification
classes.comment: The SDS section summarizing GHS classification, signal word, and the overall hazard/emergency overview of the product.

classes.label: Section 3 - Composition/Information on Ingredients
classes.comment: The SDS section listing hazardous and non-hazardous ingredients with CAS numbers, weight percentages, and GHS classifications.

classes.label: Section 4 - First Aid Measures
classes.comment: The SDS section describing recommended first-aid response for inhalation, skin contact, eye contact, and ingestion exposures.

classes.label: Section 5 - Fire-Fighting Measures
classes.comment: The SDS section covering suitable/unsuitable extinguishing media, combustion hazards, and firefighter protective equipment.

classes.label: Section 6 - Accidental Release Measures
classes.comment: The SDS section describing clean-up procedures and environmental precautions for spills or releases of the product.

classes.label: Section 7 - Handling and Storage
classes.comment: The SDS section giving guidance on safe handling practices and proper storage conditions for the product.

classes.label: Section 8 - Exposure Controls/Personal Protection
classes.comment: The SDS section listing occupational exposure limits and recommended personal protective equipment for handling the product.

classes.label: Section 9 - Physical and Chemical Properties
classes.comment: The SDS section recording measurable physical and chemical properties such as appearance, odor, density, and solubility.

classes.label: GHS Signal Word
classes.comment: The GHS word ('Danger' or 'Warning') used on a label to indicate the relative severity of a hazard.

classes.label: Skin Protection
classes.comment: PPE designed to shield the skin from contact with the product, its dust, or hot/molten material.

classes.label: Storage Requirement
classes.comment: A condition or precaution recommended for safely storing the product when not in use.
classes.example: :requirementX a sds:StorageRequirement ; rdfs:label "Store in a dry, cool area"@en .

classes.label: Substance
classes.comment: A single chemical species with one defined composition, as distinct from a multi-ingredient mixture.

classes.label: Supplier
classes.comment: The organization that supplies or distributes the product to customers, which may differ from the manufacturer.

classes.label: Target Organ System
classes.comment: A body system or organ that a chemical's toxicological effects are known to specifically affect.

classes.label: Toxicological Effect
classes.comment: A documented biological effect of the product or a component on living organisms, such as irritation or carcinogenicity.
classes.example: :effectX a sds:ToxicologicalEffect ; rdfs:label "Lung tumors observed in animal studies"@en .

classes.label: Transport Classification
classes.comment: The regulatory classification of the product for shipment under transport regulations such as DOT, IMDG, or IATA.
classes.example: :transportX a sds:TransportClassification ; sds:transportStatusText "Not regulated as hazardous for shipment"@en .

classes.label: Unsuitable Extinguishing Media
classes.comment: An extinguishing agent that is specifically discouraged because it could worsen the fire or create a hazard.

classes.label: Warning
classes.comment: GHS signal word for less severe hazard categories.

classes.label: Waste Disposal Measure
classes.comment: A recommended method for disposing of unused product, residues, or contaminated packaging.
classes.example: :measureX a sds:WasteDisposalMeasure ; rdfs:label "Dispose of in accordance with local regulations"@en .

objectProperties.label: appears in section
objectProperties.comment: Links any extracted fact, statement, or entity to the SDS section in which it was found.

objectProperties.label: classifies component
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasGHSClassification: links a GHS classification to the chemical entity it classifies.

objectProperties.label: composition component
objectProperties.comment: Links a composition record to the chemical component it describes.

objectProperties.label: contains entity
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of appearsInSection: links an SDS section to entities found within it.

objectProperties.label: describes product
objectProperties.comment: Links an SDS document to the product it describes.

objectProperties.label: has component
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a chemical component contained within it.

objectProperties.label: has composition record
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a structured composition record describing one ingredient's identity and concentration.

objectProperties.label: has ecological effect
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a documented ecological or environmental impact.

objectProperties.label: has emergency contact
objectProperties.comment: Links an SDS document to an emergency contact phone number or service.

objectProperties.label: has evidence span
objectProperties.comment: Links an extraction record to the specific source text span that justifies the extracted fact.

objectProperties.label: has exposure limit
objectProperties.comment: Links a chemical component to an occupational exposure limit value, such as an OSHA PEL or ACGIH TWA.

objectProperties.label: has extinguishing media
objectProperties.comment: Links a fire-fighting measure to the specific extinguishing agent it recommends.

objectProperties.label: has fire-fighting measure
objectProperties.comment: Links a product or fire hazard to the recommended fire-fighting response.

objectProperties.label: has first aid measure
objectProperties.comment: Links a hazard or exposure route to the recommended first-aid response.

objectProperties.label: has GHS classification
objectProperties.comment: Links a chemical component to a structured GHS classification consisting of hazard class, category, and statement.

objectProperties.label: has handling requirement
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a recommended practice for safely handling it during use or processing.

objectProperties.label: has hazard
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a hazard it presents under typical use, processing, or fire conditions.

objectProperties.label: has hazard category
objectProperties.comment: Links a GHS classification to its severity category, such as Category 2 or Category 4.

objectProperties.label: has hazard class
objectProperties.comment: Links a GHS classification to its hazard class, such as Acute Toxicity or Aquatic Chronic hazard.

objectProperties.label: has hazard statement
objectProperties.comment: Links a GHS classification to the standardized hazard statement (H-code) it carries.

objectProperties.label: has inventory status
objectProperties.comment: Links a product or chemical component to its listing status on a national chemical inventory.

objectProperties.label: has manufacturer
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to the organization that manufactures it.

objectProperties.label: has organization
objectProperties.comment: Links an SDS document to any organization (manufacturer, supplier, or other) referenced in it. Specialized by hasManufacturer and hasSupplier.

objectProperties.label: has physical or chemical property
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to one of its measured physical or chemical properties.

objectProperties.label: has pictogram
objectProperties.comment: Links a GHS classification to the hazard pictogram it displays on a label.

objectProperties.label: has precautionary statement
objectProperties.comment: Links a GHS classification or hazard to a recommended precautionary statement.

objectProperties.label: has regulatory listing
objectProperties.comment: Links a product or component to a regulatory program listing, such as SARA 313 or California Proposition 65.

objectProperties.label: has route of exposure
objectProperties.comment: Links a hazard or toxicological effect to the route by which exposure occurs, such as inhalation or skin contact.

objectProperties.label: has section
objectProperties.comment: Links an SDS document to one of its constituent sections.

objectProperties.label: has signal word
objectProperties.comment: Links a GHS classification to its associated signal word, 'Danger' or 'Warning'.

objectProperties.label: has storage requirement
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a recommended condition for its safe storage.

objectProperties.label: has supplier
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to the organization that supplies or sells it.

objectProperties.label: has target organ system
objectProperties.comment: Links a toxicological effect to the body system or organ it specifically affects.

objectProperties.label: has toxicological effect
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a documented toxicological effect on humans or animals.

objectProperties.label: has transport classification
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to its regulatory transport classification.

objectProperties.label: has waste disposal measure
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a recommended waste disposal method for unused product or residues.

objectProperties.label: is ChEBI normalization of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of normalizedToChEBI: links a ChEBI entity to the SDS chemical entity it normalises.

objectProperties.label: is combustion product of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of mayGenerateOnCombustion: links a combustion product to the substance that may generate it.

objectProperties.label: is component of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasComponent: links a chemical component to the product it is part of.

objectProperties.label: is composition component in
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of compositionComponent: links a chemical component to the composition record it appears in.

objectProperties.label: is composition record of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasCompositionRecord: links a composition record to the product whose formulation it describes.

objectProperties.label: is control measure for
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of requiresControlMeasure: links a control measure to the hazard it mitigates.

objectProperties.label: is described by
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of describesProduct: links a product to the SDS document that describes it.

objectProperties.label: is ecological effect of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasEcologicalEffect: links an ecological effect to the product that causes it.

objectProperties.label: is emergency contact of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasEmergencyContact: links an emergency contact to the SDS document that references it.

objectProperties.label: is evidence span of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasEvidenceSpan: links an evidence span to the extraction record it supports.

objectProperties.label: is exposure limit of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasExposureLimit: links an exposure limit to the chemical entity for which it is defined.

objectProperties.label: is extinguishing media for
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasExtinguishingMedia: links an extinguishing medium to the fire-fighting measure that recommends it.

objectProperties.label: is fire fighting measure of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasFireFightingMeasure: links a fire-fighting measure to the product it protects.

objectProperties.label: is handling requirement of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasHandlingRequirement: links a handling requirement to the product it applies to.

objectProperties.label: is hazard category of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasHazardCategory: links a hazard category to the GHS classification that uses it.

objectProperties.label: is hazard class of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasHazardClass: links a hazard class to the GHS classification that uses it.

objectProperties.label: is hazard of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasHazard: links a hazard to the product that presents it.

objectProperties.label: is hazard statement of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasHazardStatement: links a hazard statement (H-code) to the GHS classification that carries it.

objectProperties.label: is inventory status of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasInventoryStatus: links an inventory status to the chemical entity that holds it.

objectProperties.label: is organization of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasOrganization: links an organization to the SDS document that lists it.

objectProperties.label: is physical chemical property of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasPhysicalChemicalProperty: links a physical or chemical property to the product it characterises.

objectProperties.label: is pictogram of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasPictogram: links a GHS pictogram to the classification that requires it.

objectProperties.label: is precautionary statement of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasPrecautionaryStatement: links a precautionary statement (P-code) to the GHS classification that carries it.

objectProperties.label: is regulatory listing of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasRegulatoryListing: links a regulatory listing to the chemical entity it governs.

objectProperties.label: is section of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasSection: links an SDS section to the document it belongs to.

objectProperties.label: is signal word of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasSignalWord: links a signal word (Danger or Warning) to the GHS classification that uses it.

objectProperties.label: is storage requirement of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasStorageRequirement: links a storage requirement to the product it applies to.

objectProperties.label: is target organ system of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasTargetOrganSystem: links a target organ or system to the toxicological effect that affects it.

objectProperties.label: is thermal decomposition product of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of mayGenerateOnThermalDecomposition: links a decomposition product to the substance that may generate it on heating.

objectProperties.label: is toxicological effect of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasToxicologicalEffect: links a toxicological effect to the product that causes it.

objectProperties.label: is transport classification of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasTransportClassification: links a transport classification to the product it covers.

objectProperties.label: is waste disposal measure of
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasWasteDisposalMeasure: links a waste disposal measure to the product it applies to.

objectProperties.label: manufactures
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasManufacturer: links a manufacturer to the products it produces.

objectProperties.label: may generate on combustion
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a chemical species it may release when it burns in a fire.

objectProperties.label: may generate on thermal decomposition
objectProperties.comment: Links a product to a chemical species it may release under thermal decomposition short of full combustion.

objectProperties.label: normalized to ChEBI
objectProperties.comment: Links a chemical mention or SDS chemical entity to a ChEBI identifier when available.

objectProperties.label: requires control measure
objectProperties.comment: Links a hazard to a control measure recommended to mitigate it.

objectProperties.label: requires PPE
objectProperties.comment: Links a hazard, task, or product to the personal protective equipment recommended when handling it.

objectProperties.label: supplies
objectProperties.comment: Inverse of hasSupplier: links a supplier to the products it distributes.

datatypeProperties.label: address
datatypeProperties.comment: The physical mailing or facility address of an organization mentioned in the SDS.

datatypeProperties.label: CAS number
datatypeProperties.comment: The Chemical Abstracts Service registry number uniquely identifying a chemical entity.

datatypeProperties.label: concentration lower bound
datatypeProperties.comment: The lower numeric bound of a component's weight-percent concentration range in a composition record.

datatypeProperties.label: concentration upper bound
datatypeProperties.comment: The upper numeric bound of a component's weight-percent concentration range in a composition record.

datatypeProperties.label: confidence score
datatypeProperties.comment: A numeric score indicating how confident an extraction process is that an extracted fact is correct.

datatypeProperties.label: EC number
datatypeProperties.comment: The European Community number that uniquely identifies a chemical substance under EU regulations.

datatypeProperties.label: email address
datatypeProperties.comment: An email address associated with an organization or contact mentioned in the SDS.

datatypeProperties.label: GHS code
datatypeProperties.comment: The alphanumeric GHS code identifying a specific hazard (H-code) or precautionary (P-code) statement.

datatypeProperties.label: hazard statement text
datatypeProperties.comment: The full text of a GHS hazard statement corresponding to its H-code.

datatypeProperties.label: phone number
datatypeProperties.comment: A telephone number associated with an organization or emergency contact mentioned in the SDS.

datatypeProperties.label: precautionary statement text
datatypeProperties.comment: The full text of a GHS precautionary statement describing a recommended risk-reduction action.

datatypeProperties.label: print date
datatypeProperties.comment: The date on which the SDS document was printed or generated for distribution.

datatypeProperties.label: product code
datatypeProperties.comment: The manufacturer's internal code or catalog identifier for the specific product grade.

datatypeProperties.label: product name
datatypeProperties.comment: The official or display name of the product as stated in the SDS.

datatypeProperties.label: recommended use
datatypeProperties.comment: The intended application or use case for the product as stated by the manufacturer.

datatypeProperties.label: regulatory status text
datatypeProperties.comment: The free-text description of a product's or component's status under a specific regulatory listing.

datatypeProperties.label: revision date
datatypeProperties.comment: The date on which the SDS document was most recently revised.

datatypeProperties.label: revision number
datatypeProperties.comment: The sequential revision number identifying which version of the SDS document this is.

datatypeProperties.label: source page
datatypeProperties.comment: The page number of the SDS document where a given fact or entity was found.

datatypeProperties.label: source text
datatypeProperties.comment: The verbatim text segment from the SDS document that an extracted fact or entity was derived from.

datatypeProperties.label: trade name
datatypeProperties.comment: The trademarked brand name under which the product is marketed.

datatypeProperties.label: transport status text
datatypeProperties.comment: The free-text description of a product's transport regulatory status as stated in the SDS.

datatypeProperties.label: website
datatypeProperties.comment: A web address associated with the manufacturer, supplier, or product mentioned in the SDS.

datatypeProperties.label: weight percent
datatypeProperties.comment: The concentration of a chemical component in a product, expressed as a percentage by weight (often a range).
